name: MCP73871T-2CCI_ML
title: Single-cell Li-Ion/Li-Polymer linear charger with system load sharing (power path)
summary: The MCP73871 is a linear charger for one Li-Ion or Li-Polymer cell with a built-in power path: it runs a system load from a USB port or AC-DC adapter while charging the cell, and switches the load to the battery through an ideal diode when input is missing or cannot supply it. It does CC/CV charging with preconditioning, PROG3-set termination, automatic recharge, a safety timer, thermistor monitoring and die-temperature regulation. Input current is held to 100 mA or 500 mA for USB or 1.65 A typical for an adapter, and input-voltage proportional control backs off charge current when the source sags. Charge voltage (4.10, 4.20, 4.35 or 4.40 V), timer and low-battery threshold are fixed by the part number; the MCP73871T-2CCI/ML is 4.20 V, 6 hours, LBO at 3.1 V, in a 4 x 4 mm QFN-20 on tape and reel.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: System supply output, fed from IN or from the battery. Decouple to VSS with at least 4.7 μF.

pins.name: VPCC
pins.function: Input-voltage sense for voltage proportional charge control (1.23 V threshold). Tie to IN to switch the feature off.

pins.name: SEL
pins.function: Input source type: low for a USB port, high for an AC-DC adapter.

pins.name: PROG2
pins.function: USB input current limit when SEL is low: low gives 100 mA, high gives 500 mA.

pins.name: THERM
pins.function: Battery thermistor connection; sources the 50 μA bias current and senses the resulting voltage.

pins.name: PG
pins.function: Power good, active low: pulled low while the input is above UVLO and above the battery voltage.

pins.name: STAT1/LBO
pins.function: Charge status output 1; on LBO options it also signals a low battery while VBAT > VIN.

pins.name: TE
pins.function: Timer enable, active low: low runs the safety timer, high stops it.

pins.name: VSS
pins.function: Ground reference for the battery, the system load and the input. The exposed pad is tied to VSS inside and must be at VSS potential on the board.

pins.name: PROG3
pins.function: Resistor to VSS sets the charge termination current, for adapter and USB input alike.

pins.name: PROG1
pins.function: Resistor to VSS sets the fast charge current with SEL high, and the preconditioning current for both input types.

pins.name: VBAT
pins.function: Battery positive terminal: charge current out, discharge current in. Decouple to VSS with at least 4.7 μF.

pins.name: VBAT_SENSE
pins.function: Battery voltage sense; the charger regulates this pin to VREG. Connect to the battery positive terminal.

pins.name: CE
pins.function: Charge enable: high enables charging, low disables it. 1.8 V logic compatible.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Supply input from a USB port or an AC-DC adapter. Decouple to VSS with at least 4.7 μF.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: Stand-alone charger and power path from one USB or adapter input. VPCC is strapped to IN, so input-voltage proportional control is off. OUT feeds the system load and VBAT the single cell, each with 4.7 µF to ground; the input carries 10 µF. RPROG1 and RPROG3 set the fast charge and termination currents, a 10 kΩ NTC on THERM watches cell temperature, and three LEDs with 470 Ω resistors from IN show PG, STAT2 and STAT1/LBO. SEL, PROG2, TE and CE are each driven to a fixed low or high level.

circuits.title: Typical stand-alone application circuit with VPCC
circuits.description: The same charger fed from a 5 V adapter or USB port, with input-voltage proportional charge control in use. A 330 kΩ / 110 kΩ divider from IN reaches the 1.23 V VPCC threshold as IN falls toward 5 V, and from there charge current is reduced to hold the input up. An SMAJ5.0A/AC transient suppressor across the input clamps hot-plug spikes. The rest matches the typical circuit: 10 µF on IN, 4.7 µF on OUT and on VBAT, RPROG1 and RPROG3 to ground, a 10 kΩ NTC on THERM, three LEDs with 470 Ω resistors, and logic levels on SEL, PROG2, TE and CE.

operation.text: Two internal paths meet at OUT: a current-limited pass FET from IN, and a FET from VBAT that acts as an ideal diode (synchronous switch). A separate charge FET runs from the input side to VBAT. The system on OUT is served first and the battery gets what current is left, so the system can start on a deeply discharged or missing cell and the cell sees fewer charge and discharge cycles. With no input, OUT runs from the battery.

SEL high treats the input as an AC-DC adapter: total input current (system plus charge) is limited to 1.8 A, 1.65 A typical, and fast charge current is set by the PROG1 resistor. SEL low treats it as a USB port and holds total input current inside the USB limits chosen by PROG2: low for 100 mA, high for 500 mA.

When input current reaches its limit the charge current is reduced first, keeping the system load supplied. Current to the system is not actively limited: if the system asks for more than the input can give, the ideal diode conducts and the battery makes up the difference.

If the input sags because of source impedance or current limit until the divider voltage on VPCC falls to 1.23 V, charge current is cut back to hold the input there; the system keeps priority and the battery helps carry the load if needed. It works the same with USB or adapter input. Connecting VPCC to IN disables it.

UVLO is always active. The device stays in shutdown until the input exceeds the UVLO threshold and, with a battery present, sits about 100 mV above the battery voltage; it returns to shutdown when the input falls within about 100 mV of VBAT. Battery reverse discharge current during UVLO is below 2 μA.

A charge cycle starts only once UVLO is satisfied and either a cell or a load sits on the output. With SEL high a PROG1 resistor to VSS is required; with SEL low PROG2 must be driven high or low. No logic input may be left floating.
Below the factory-set preconditioning threshold (VPTH/VREG, 72 % typical) the cell is charged at 10 % of the PROG1 fast charge current. Above it, the charger moves to constant current.

In fast charge the PROG1 current flows to the battery or load and the timer is reset at entry. When VBAT reaches VREG the charger holds the voltage at VREG (4.10, 4.20, 4.35 or 4.40 V by option, ±0.5 %) while current tapers.

The cycle ends when the averaged charge current falls below the PROG3 threshold or the safety timer runs out; the charge is then latched off in Charge Complete. A 1 ms filter on the termination comparator rides through load transients. In Charge Complete VBAT is watched, and a fall below the recharge threshold (VREG – 0.15 V typical) starts a new cycle.

The timer period is set by the option code (disabled, 4, 6 or 8 hours). TE low enables the timer and TE high disables it; stopping the timer through TE does not reset it, and cycling CE does. If the timer expires in fast charge before the recharge threshold is reached, the cycle stops with a timer fault until the battery is removed; the device then waits in standby for a new battery. TE accepts 1.8 V logic.
CE high enables the charger and CE low disables it while the power path stays active. A floating CE during charging can make the system unstable. CE accepts 1.8 V logic.

During charge a regulated 50 μA source on THERM biases a 10 kΩ NTC (or PTC) thermistor, and the THERM voltage is compared with 1.24 V and 0.25 V. Outside that window the charge FET turns off and the timer holds its count; charging resumes when the voltage returns. Series and parallel resistors around the thermistor move the window. Without a thermistor, a plain 10 kΩ resistor between THERM and ground keeps charging enabled.

Charge current is cut back according to die temperature under high power or high ambient conditions. As a second line of protection, charging stops above 150 °C die temperature and resumes after it cools about 10 °C.

STAT1, STAT2 and PG are open-drain outputs that sink current only, for LEDs or a pull-up to a microcontroller input. PG pulls low while the input is above UVLO and above VBAT. PG must not be pulled above VIN, because a diode path leads back to VIN.
On LBO options (third code character B, C or D) STAT1 also goes low while OUT is supplied by the cell and VBAT drops below the LBO threshold of 3.0, 3.1 or 3.2 V. Option A has no LBO.

Charge rate follows the battery vendor's recommendation; for example a 1000 mAh pack charged at 0.7C, 700 mA, charges fastest without harming the cell. The device dissipates most just after leaving preconditioning, at the highest input voltage, so charge current, cost and heat are traded against each other.

The loop stays stable whether a cell is fitted or not. At least 4.7 μF from VBAT to VSS keeps the constant voltage loop stable with no battery and offsets the inductance of the pack and its wiring. Ceramic, tantalum or aluminium electrolytic parts of 4.7 μF work for charge currents up to 1000 mA, with no minimum ESR.
A shorted or failed input cannot pull the battery down: the internal pass device's body diode is blocked from discharging the cell into IN.

The recommended system load is 1.0 A or the cell's maximum discharge rate, whichever is lower. The ideal diode from VBAT to OUT can carry up to 2 A, and thermal shutdown may turn the device off at high current.

A hot-pluggable input such as a USB cable or wall supply needs a transient suppressor from the input connector's positive line to ground, since cable inductance produces large spikes on plugging and unplugging. A unidirectional or bidirectional part may be used.

Place the battery close to the VBAT and VSS pins to keep drops in the high-current traces small. Using the board as a heat sink, many vias in the exposed-pad land carry heat to the far copper layers and lower junction temperature.
